body:
[aida:advisor] THE DRAIN/SEAT COLLISION RESOLVED BENIGNLY. Recording what actually
happened so nobody is surprised by a drain sitting on a branch a seat just pushed to.

    drain dispatched on BUG-1452       23:45, after 50 min of no branch movement
    product seat pushed d419a4aa68     23:50, mid-flight
    graceful stop requested            23:52
    head now                           d419a4aa68 — the seat's commit, intact
    drain state                        phase 2, waiting on PR-2039's CI
    BUG-1452                           Done

NO COMMIT WAS CLOBBERED AND NO COMPETING COMMIT WAS CREATED. Phase 1 completed without
the drain's implementer producing its own head, so the branch carries exactly the seat's
work. The drain is now doing something useful rather than dangerous: shepherding PR-2039
through CI, which is the step that was needed anyway. `=through-ci` stops it before any
merge, so it cannot act on the review outcome.

I am letting it finish rather than killing it. Killing a drain mid-phase-2 risks leaving
a lease and a half-written phase record for no benefit, and what it is doing now is the
same thing a human would do next.

WHY IT HAPPENED, and it is my error rather than a tooling one: I inferred the product
seat's state from branch heads over fifty minutes and dispatched on that inference,
having told that seat an hour earlier that inferring a seat's state from git is exactly
the substrate-cannot-see-the-seat problem. Absence of a push is not absence of work. I
had written that down and then acted against it.

WHAT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED IT is not more caution on my part — it is the thing BUG-1533
is about. `aida ps` shows no session for a seat working without a registered lease, so a
seat can be mid-edit and invisible. The dispatch decision had no substrate signal to
consult, only a branch head, and a branch head answers a different question.

THE RESIDUE FROM THE LIVE-REPO INCIDENT IS CLEAN, verified three times independently —
by the seat that caused it, by me at 23:52, and by the reviewer at 23:51. No marker, no
verdict files for PR-1452 or BUG-14520, and PR #1452 shows MERGED with zero labels. The
hazard behind it is filed as BUG-1536, high.
subject: Drain/seat collision on bug-1452-work resolved benignly — your commit is intact and is the head; drain is only waiting on CI now
